shacks = 12

scenes.narration: In Python, a name is like a tag tied to a value. Shacks is a tag on twelve. Open underscore shacks is a tag on nine. When you write shacks, Python follows the tag to find the value. Remember this picture. It explains many puzzles later.

scenes.onScreen: shacks.py again with the output panel on the right

Four: the last line names the error, and often suggests the fix. Say these four rules out loud, and you can handle most beginner errors. Try it on the shacks program, line by line.

bug.error:
Python output (exactly as Python prints it):

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "shacks.py", line 2, in <module>
    print("Shacks:", shack)
                     ^^^^^
NameError: name 'shack' is not defined. Did you mean: 'shacks'?
bug.why: Read a traceback from the bottom: the last line names the error and often suggests the fix, and the line above it shows where it happened.

shorts.title: Sticky notes for code
shorts.script: The line Python ignores. A hash sign makes a comment. Python skips it completely, but the next human reads it, and that human might be you, next month. Good comments say why you did something, not what the code does. The code already shows what it does. Write a comment above any line that surprises you, and keep it short. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Comment your code.

shorts.title: Names are tags
shorts.hook: "A name is a tag on a value."
shorts.script: A name is a tag on a value. Shacks is a tag on twelve. Open underscore shacks is a tag on nine. When you write shacks in your code, Python follows the tag to find the value. Names are not boxes that hold things. They are tags that point at things. Keep this picture in mind, because it explains a lot later. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Names as tags.

shorts.title: Underscores in names
shorts.script: Open underscore shacks, not open shacks. A name can have letters, digits and underscores, but never spaces. It cannot start with a digit either. Pick names that say what they hold, so you can read your program like a sentence. Shacks and open underscore shacks tell a clear story. Short, clear names make every bug easier to find. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Name things well.

shorts.title: Read a traceback
shorts.script: Start at the bottom. When Python stops with a traceback, read it from the last line up. The last line names the error and often suggests the fix. The line above shows where it happened. Python even asks, did you mean, and offers the correct spelling. Read the hint before you change anything. Then you fix bugs much faster. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bottom first.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.script: A comment that lied. I wrote, this works, and the traceback disagreed. Your challenge. Write a program with a comment at the top. Make two names, boys and girls, with any numbers you like. Then print the total number of students. Use a plus sign to add them. Share your answer in the comments below. Keep coding, says Xecxec! Full video: EP 04.
